To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CaMBD/CAM/Ca2+ complex structure shows how CaM wraps around the CaMBD and how Ca2+ binding to the CaM N-terminal lobe induces a conformational change that allows the channel to open.
the SK channel CaM-binding domain forms an elongated CaM dimer with each CaM molecule wrapping around three helices, two from each CaMBD subunits.
the structure of the SK Ca2+ binding domain (CaMB) in complex with CaM provides insight into the gating of Ca2+-activated channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function and regulation of the SK channels.
the structural basis of ion channel function, and in particular, the gating mechanism of small-conductance Ca(2+) activated potassium channels (SK channels).
the structural biology and biophysics of the small conductance calcium activated potassium (SK) channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SK channel CaM-binding domain dimerizes and binds two Ca2+-loaded CaM molecules, with the Ca2+ binding to the N-lobe.
the structure reveals the molecular basis of the CaMBD/CAM complex, and that this complex is the basis for the Ca2+-gating mechanism of SK channels.
the CaMBD/CAM complex structure provides the first structural insight of SK channels, which is the only known Ca2+-activated channel that is not voltage dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have solved the structure of the SK Ca2+ binding domain (SK-CaMBD) and its complex with Ca2+/CaM at a 1.6 Å resolution.
the Ca2+-dependent conformational change of CaM is transduced into a conformational change in the SK channel, which in turn leads to the opening of the channel.
the structure provides the first atomic-level view of Ca2+-activated channel gating.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SK channel complex is a dimer of CaM dimers, which is consistent with the idea of a CaM dimer as the functional unit of CaM.

the CaMBD/Cam complex forms a stable dimeric structure, and the CaM molecule is bound to the CaMBD in an extended conformation with the C-terminus of the N-lobe in close proximity to the N-terminus of C-lobe, which provides the basis for the proposed mechanism.
CaM can simultaneously bind to multiple proteins and, through its N- and C-terminal domains, can act as a molecular switch to regulate multiple protein functions.
